title: Agents and tools: when the model acts instead of just answering

videos.script: An assistant that checks the date, does a sum or searches a handbook seems to have hands. {{hands}} It has none. A model writes text, and that is all it can do. {{text}} What it can write is a request. Run this tool, with this input. {{request}} A program around the model reads that line, decides whether it is allowed, runs the tool, and puts the result back into the text. {{program}} Then the model is asked again, with the result in front of it. A model in that loop is what people call an agent. {{agent}} In this lesson you run the loop on the workbench. The model's turns are written for you, because no model is reachable from here. The loop and the tools are real. {{workbench}} You will see a tool that does not exist, a tool that is not allowed, and a run that hits its step limit. {{limits}} Each one is decided by the program, not by the model. {{program2}}
